feedback.problem: The number of subscribers $S(t)$ to a new video streaming service after $t$ weeks can be modeled by the differential equation ${S}^{′}(t)=0.11S(t).$ If the streaming service had $60\,000$ subscribers after $20$ weeks, calculate the number of subscribers after $32$ weeks.
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
S(t)={S}_{0}\,{e}^{0.11t},
$$

where ${S}_{0}$ is the initial number of subscribers.

We are given that after $20$ weeks, $60\,000$ people subscribed to the service. So, substituting $t=20$ and $S(20)=60\,000$ into our general solution and solving for ${S}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S(20) & ={S}_{0}\,{e}^{0.11\cdot 20} \\ 60\,000 & ={S}_{0}\,{e}^{2.2} \\ {S}_{0} & =\frac{60\,000}{{e}^{2.2}} \\  & ≈6\,648.190,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Hence, our particular solution is

$$
S(t)=6\,648.190\,{e}^{0.11t}.
$$

We want to find the number of subscribers after $32$ weeks. So, substituting $t=32$ into our particular solution, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S(32) & =6\,648.190\,{e}^{0.11\cdot 32} \\  & =6\,648.190\,{e}^{3.52} \\  & ≈224\,605,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest whole number. 

Therefore, the streaming service will have about $224\,605$ subscribers after $32$ weeks.
